title: Cap. XI: Hunnius’s ἀτοπία; counterfeit Pelagians and the needless second sin
pass_a_gloss: So, setting aside these witnesses who do not favor him, Garissoles turns to the Pelagians, and wonders at Aegidius Hunnius's ἀτοπία (absurdity), who contended that this was the Pelagians' opinion — that Adam's sin is imputed to posterity. He also wonders that a learned man (he means Placeus) hallucinated in the same matter, speaking thus about this business in a certain private Letter. Those who first invented the immediate imputation of Adam's sin (note: immediate — for this alone, and by no means the mediate, Placeus has constantly rejected) were Pelagians, who by this device tried to dodge the force of the anathemas hurled against Pelagius. For they denied hereditary corruption, that is, original sin; and to dazzle the Church's eyes they honored with that name the guilt of Adam's first sin imputed. Garissoles cries that this is false. Yet he admits that those who defined the whole account of original sin by the sole imputation of Adam's sin are to be classed with the Pelagians — classed not because they posited imputation, but because they denied corruption, and so on. That confirms Hunnius's and Placeus's opinion rather than overturns it. For they did not ascribe the dogma of immediate imputation of the first sin to Pelagius himself or to all Pelagians, but only to those who, while truly Pelagians, wanted not to seem Pelagians — for which purpose the dogma of Adam's sin imputed would have been useless if Pelagius had openly put it forward. For when they saw that those who denied original sin were held for heretics, they professed to believe original sin; but by that name they understood not propagated sin, as all the rest of the orthodox, but Adam's actual sin imputed to all. Certainly those very ones who urge immediate imputation against Placeus, though unwittingly, still cannot avoid coming near the Pelagians — as I have already observed several times in Garissoles himself. For once a propagated or inherent sin is granted that is truly sin and enough to damn us, what need is there of another sin imputed to us? Once mediate imputation of Adam's first actual sin is granted, what need of the immediate? And how can the immediate be proved from Scripture?
pass_b_english: Setting aside those unhelpful witnesses, Garissoles turns to the Pelagians and marvels at Aegidius Hunnius's ἀτοπία — Hunnius's claim that the Pelagian view was that Adam's sin is imputed to posterity. He also marvels that a learned man (he means Placeus) 'hallucinated' the same way in a private letter. Those who first invented the immediate imputation of Adam's sin — note: immediate; Placeus has always rejected that alone, never the mediate — were Pelagians trying to dodge the anathemas aimed at Pelagius. They denied hereditary corruption, that is, original sin, and to dazzle the Church they gave that name to the guilt of Adam's first sin as imputed. Garissoles cries that this is false; yet he admits that anyone who makes the whole account of original sin nothing but the imputation of Adam's sin belongs with the Pelagians — not because they taught imputation, but because they denied corruption. That confirms Hunnius and Placeus more than it overturns them. They never pinned immediate imputation of the first sin on Pelagius himself or on every Pelagian, but only on those who were truly Pelagians and wanted not to look it — for if Pelagius had openly taught imputed Adam's sin, that dodge would have been useless. Seeing that deniers of original sin were counted heretics, they professed to believe original sin, but meant by it not propagated sin, as all the orthodox do, but Adam's actual sin imputed to everyone. Indeed those who press immediate imputation against Placeus cannot help sliding toward the Pelagians, as I have already noted more than once in Garissoles himself: once a propagated, inherent sin that is truly sin and enough to damn us is granted, what need is there of another sin imputed to us? Once mediate imputation of Adam's first actual sin is granted, what need of the immediate — and how can Scripture prove it?
source_text: His ergo missis sibi non faventibus accedit D. G. ad Pelagianos, & miratur Aegidii Hunnii ἀτοπίαν, pertendentis hanc fuisse Pelagianorum sententiam, Adami peccatum posteris imputari. Miratur etiam hallucinatum in eadem re virum doctum (Placeum designat) ita de hoc negotio in privata quadam Epistola loquentem. Qui primi immediatam (nota immediatam: hanc enim solam, minime vero mediatam, Placeus constanter improbavit) imputationem peccati Adae commenti sunt, ii Pelagiani fuerunt, qui hac ratione conati sunt anathematum adversus Pelagium vibratorum impetum declinare. Negarunt enim corruptionem haereditariam, id est, originale peccatum: & ad praestringendos Ecclesiae oculos, hoc nomine donaverunt reatum imputati primi Adae peccati. Hoc D. G. falsum esse clamat. Fatetur tamen eos qui totam rationem peccati originalis sola imputatione peccati Adae definierunt, Pelagianis accensendos esse: sed accensendos, non quia imputationem posuerint, sed quia corruptionem negaverint, &c. Id quod Aegidii Hunnii & Placei sententiam confirmat potius quam evertit. Non enim dogma de imputatione primi peccati immediata ipsi Pelagio aut omnibus Pelagianis ascripserunt: Sed illis duntaxat, qui cum essent revera Pelagiani, voluerunt non Pelagiani videri: quam ad rem inutile fuisset dogma de imputato Adae peccato, si id Pelagius aperte protulisset. Cum enim viderent, qui negarent peccatum originale pro haereticis haberi, professi sunt se peccatum originale credere: sed hoc nomine non peccatum propagatum, ut reliqui omnes orthodoxi, sed peccatum actuale Adami omnibus imputatum intelligebant. Certe illi ipsi, qui adversus Placeum imputationem immediatam urgent, imprudentes quidem, sed tamen evitare non possunt, quin Pelagianis accedant; uti jam in ipso D. Garissolio aliquoties observavi. Posito enim peccato propagato seu inhaerente, quod vere peccatum sit, ac nobis damnandis sufficiat, quid opus est alio peccato nobis imputato? posita imputatione primi Adae peccati actualis mediata, quid opus est immediata? & quomodo potest immediata ex Scriptura probari?
